schematic_description: The pipeline runs left to right in four stages. Two kinds of input enter on the left: the primary data sources (RCSB, AlphaFold DB, UniProt, InterPro), and separately the validation datasets that serve as ground truth, of which 11 of 13 resolved. Stage 1, acquisition, catalogued 52,821 entries into priority tiers using httpx and tenacity. Stage 2, geometry, analysed 52,586 entries with gemmi and FreeSASA and found 239,485 bridges, with 235 entries failing. Stage 3, scan and triage, used DSSP and fpocket to produce 21,717 degron candidates, 650 triaged ligases and 1,650 scored lysines. Stage 4 trains BINMAN-LM with mlx-lm, which does text work only and never emits a number. Four modules leave on the right: Glue Atlas, Degron Scan, E3 Triage and Degradability.

worked_example.honest_note: This record was chosen because every stage that has run worked on it. A reader should look at the misses list and the novel-bridge set in FINDINGS.md for the cases where stages did not.

validation.note: A metric whose dataset is unavailable is reported as computed: false with the reason. Nothing here is estimated, and no hand-written control was substituted for a missing published one (spec 4.1b).

metrics_not_computed.reason: The atlas `substrate_count` column is populated from the UbiBrowser literature set itself, so a Spearman correlation against UbiBrowser would be a tautology (rho = 1 by construction) rather than a test. A genuine version needs a second, independent substrate source.

artefact_precision.note: Measured over the artefact CCDs present in the atlas. The held-out-split figure in FINDINGS.md (0.927) is the one to quote: it was measured on a half of the list that the classification rules were not developed against.

misses.note: Each is a sensitivity bug. Enumerated with its reason in FINDINGS.md.

sensitivity.source: Sievers et al. 2018 (10.1126/science.aat0572), supplementary data files S2 and S6 pooled: 32 zinc fingers depleted under IMiD treatment at FDR < 0.05 against 5476 assayed in the same screens and not depleted. Spec 9.2 names the Molecular Cell 2025 and Nature Communications 2025 screens; neither resolved, and this is the same experimental design (one flow-cytometry screen supplying both arms) from a source that did.

specificity.source: Sievers et al. 2018 (10.1126/science.aat0572), supplementary data files S2 and S6 pooled: 32 zinc fingers depleted under IMiD treatment at FDR < 0.05 against 5476 assayed in the same screens and not depleted. Spec 9.2 names the Molecular Cell 2025 and Nature Communications 2025 screens; neither resolved, and this is the same experimental design (one flow-cytometry screen supplying both arms) from a source that did.

contingency_table.note: Rows are the screen, columns the geometric filter. A zinc finger is 'called' when a degron candidate on its AlphaFold model shares at least 1 residue(s) with the assayed window. 155 assayed zinc fingers were excluded because their protein never reached the scan (no AlphaFold model, or outside the reviewed human proteome) and 0 for want of a usable accession or window; a miss there is missing data, not a false negative, so neither is scored.

roc_auc.note: Over degron_geometry_score, taking the best overlapping candidate per zinc finger and zero where the protein was scanned and nothing overlapped. The score is therefore heavily tied at zero, which caps the AUC achievable by ranking alone: read it with the contingency table, not instead of it.

threshold_sweep.note: Spec 9.6 allows one documented threshold adjustment before G6, and D-010 already spent it on five documented degrons, with no matched negative set in existence at the time. This sweep asks whether a second adjustment could even help: if no cut on degron_geometry_score clears both floors together, the cut is not what is wrong and moving it would be tuning against the test set.

missed_zinc_fingers.note: candidates_on_protein is how many degron candidates the scan found anywhere on that protein: a non-zero count with no overlap means the filter fired, but elsewhere.

value.calibration_basis: measured geometry of 5 documented CRBN/DCAF neosubstrate degrons

calibration.note: Calibrated to the measured geometry of five documented CRBN and DCAF degrons, as the single adjustment spec 9.6 permits (DECISIONS D-010). Not independently validated: see the reason above.

missed.IKZF3 Gly155: relative SASA 0.15, buried in the monomer model
missed.RBM39 Gly268: in a helix, not a hairpin, in the monomer model

documented_degron_recovery.note: A method sanity check, NOT the spec 9.2 metric: the set is small, it was used for calibration, and it contains no negatives.

rank_enrichment_p.note: One-sided Mann-Whitney on the triage score. `exploitation_status` and `has_ligand` are not weighted components of the score, so the test is not circular.

substrate_spearman.reason: The atlas `substrate_count` column is populated from the UbiBrowser literature set itself, so a Spearman correlation against UbiBrowser would be a tautology (rho = 1 by construction) rather than a test. A genuine version needs a second, independent substrate source.

9.4.title: Degradability

held_out_auc.source: UniProt CROSSLNK ubiquitin isopeptide annotations for the reviewed human proteome (950 observed sites on 403 proteins, 11755 unannotated lysines as negatives), measured on a protein-level split with 338 observed sites held out.
held_out_auc.note: **Accessibility only.** This is the AUC of lysine NZ relative accessibility as a predictor of whether a lysine carries an observed ubiquitylation site. The three Cb-Cb reach boundaries are unfitted and no reach verdict is emitted: an AlphaFold monomer carrying an observed site has no ligand site for the distance to be measured from. The negatives are lysines with no annotation, not lysines assayed and found unmodified, so this is a weaker construction than the matched screen behind 9.2.

protein_level_split_honoured.note: A protein contributes wholly to train or wholly to test: 135 of 403 proteins were held out.

window_fitted.note: The fit ran but its held-out AUC misses the floor, so nothing was written back: spec 5.4 forbids a starting value surviving into a shipped config unless the fit lands on it.

honest_limits: Observed ubiquitylation sites come from native E3 biology, not from induced ternary complexes, so the window would be a proxy even once fitted.
Absence of a reported site is weak evidence that a lysine is unusable: detection is incomplete and condition-dependent, which biases the negative set.
An AUC of 0.65 to 0.75 here would be a genuine and useful result. Anything above 0.9 should be treated as suspected leakage and investigated before it is believed.
